Q: What is a scoville unit?

A: A Scoville Heat Unit (SHU) system was created by the chemist Wilbur Scoville in 1912. Scoville units are determined by a pepper's capsaicin concentration, which can be measured using the original Scoville Organoleptic Test where human tasters determine the amount of sugar water needed to dilute a pepper's heat to a non-detectable level, or more accurately today with High-Performance Liquid Chromatography (HPLC), a scientific method that measures the exact capsaicin content in a pepper. The SHU rating corresponds to the number of times the capsaicin needs to be diluted to remove the "burn". 

Q: What is capsaicin?

A: An active component of chili peppers, the burn you get in your mouth from peppers is from the capsaicin (pronounced like CAP SAY SIN), which is a chemical compound found within the pepper.  It activates pain receptors in your mouth called TRVP1, that are triggered by heat, which sends signals to the brain that you are experiencing a painful, hot sensation, even though there's no actual damage being done.  Even though it burns, there are possible medical advantages of it, like helping with pain, supporting heart health and pain loss.  See, it's not ALL bad!

Q: Why don't you list the scoville units on your items?

A: Scoville Units are subjective.  No one pepper has the exact same amount of heat as the other, so while we can give a range of what the DRY pepper is from its scoville rating, when you add other ingredients like vinegar and water, for instance, it dilutes the sting of the pepper.  Some of our items may have a scoville unit listed for the shock value, but remember that we're highlighting what the DRY pepper rating is, not the hot sauce rating.

Q: Why are the seeds from hot sauces or peppers so hot?

A: That's a common misconception that isn't true.  The actual seeds aren't hot, it's what is surrounding them that's hot.  The white, fleshy part of the inside of the pepper is where the oils are. The capsaicin, that is where the heat is, and the seeds are touching it all the time, which makes them seem like they are hot.

Q: Are dark hot sauces always hotter?

A: That's another myth.  Hot sauce colors are determined by the peppers and any other colors from other ingredients such as flavoring, different colored peppers, vinegar, spices, fruits, and the aging and fermentation process (the longer they sit in an oak barrel, the darker they can get).  Although many sauces that are dark ARE hot, it's not the case with all darker hot sauces.

Q: I don't see the hot sauce I like here.  Can you get it in for me?

A: Most likely, yes.  You can e mail us at cs@hottimesauces.com and inquire about special ordering.  Keep in mind that special orders often require a minimum amount of sauces to be ordered, along with shipping costs.

Q: Do hot sauces have to be refrigerated?

A: The majority of hot sauces do not need refrigeration.  Some companies recommend refrigeration to preserve freshness which will help it keep its color and to keep the flavor and the heat of the sauce at a premium level.  It also depends on how much you intend on using the sauce.  When dabbing your sauce on food, try not to let the opening of the bottle touch the food, as this can contaminate the opening and get in to the hot sauce inside the bottle, which is one major reason why companies recommend refrigerating hot sauces, because food contamination slows when hot sauce is refrigerated.  Note that SOME fermented hot sauces do require refrigeration or the constant fermenting at room temperature may cause the hot sauce to erupt through the top of the bottle.  It is recommended by Hot Time Sauces that you follow the instructions on the label when it pertains to refrigerating your sauces.

Q: Why should I shake the bottle before I use the hot sauce?

A: Ingredients tend to separate as the bottle is still.  Peppers and spices, which are the heavier ingredients, will sink to the bottom as any vinegar stays at the top.  Shaking the bottle gets the ingredients back together for optimum freshness, consistency and taste. Separation of ingredients is 100 percent normal for any hot sauce, and shaking the bottle is always recommended before consuming your product.

Q: Is the "best by" date on a hot sauce bottle the expiration date?

A: Not at all.  The "best by" date is just telling you that the hot sauce is at its freshest before the date comes along.  Hot sauce will often last 6 months to a year, or more, after the best by date has gone by, especially if you have not opened it.  You can tell when a hot sauce has officially expired by smell, consistency differences and of course, mold.  If you have not refrigerated your sauce(s) before the best by date has approached, it is probably best to do so afterwards to preserve the sauce(s) for a longer amount of time.

Return Eligibility

The return window is 14 days.  To be eligible for a return, your item must be unopened (seal not broken), in its original packaging and undamaged.  Initial shipping charges (when you placed your order) are not refundable.  The buyer also pays for return shipping and is responsible for the proper packaging to ensure the item(s) does not arrive to us broken.  Items sent back to us without first requesting a return will not be accepted.  Unfortunately, we cannot accept returns on sale items, clearance items or e-gift cards.

You can always contact us for any return questions at cs@hottimesauces.com

Refunds

If anything in your order arrives broken, we will need your order number and a picture of the package and the broken item(s) e-mailed to us as soon as possible at cs@hottimesauces.com.  The more pictures you send, the better, for insurance purposes.  

The order will be replaced if we have the same item in stock.  If not, a refund will be granted. 

We will notify you once we’ve received and inspected your return, and let you know if the refund was approved or not. If approved, you’ll be automatically refunded on your original payment method within 5 business days (excluding holidays and weekends). Keep in mind that it can take some time for your bank or credit card company to process and post the refund. If more than 10 business days have passed since we’ve approved your return and you have not been credited back, please contact us at cs@hottimesauces.com

Hot Time Sauces Disclaimer And Product Waiver

Some of our sauces are extremely hot.  By purchasing any of our sauces, you are acknowledging that upon consumption, you may experience physical discomfort, illness or injury. Hot Time Sauces is not liable for any potential harm that may come to you as a result of consuming our products, as you are doing so at your own risk with the understanding that some sauces are very hot. By purchasing our products, you are releasing Hot Time Sauces from any liabilities that my occur from consuming our products.

For Domestic (US) Shipping

Shipping Rates & Policies 

We strive to ship as fast as possible. We do not ship on weekends or holidays. Your order will ship the same day provided you place the order before 9:00 AM MST.

Domestic US Shipping Rates & Policies

Orders composed entirely of standard 5 oz bottles ship free at $70 or more. (not including package deals)

Orders containing larger bottles (over 5 oz) or mixed bottle sizes ship free at $80 or more. (not including package deals)

Orders under the free shipping threshold ship for a flat rate of $8.50 to $10.50 based on total weight.

Single 5 oz bottles ship for an $8.50 flat rate.

Standard free shipping is delivered via USPS Ground Advantage (3 to 8 business days), though alternative carriers may be used at our discretion.

Package deals do not qualify for free shipping regardless of the order total.

Free shipping cannot be combined with percentage-off discount codes; applying a promo code will revert shipping to standard rates.

Expedited & Alternative Shipping

USPS Priority Mail (2 to 3 business days) is available at a flat rate of $16.00.

USPS Express Mail rates calculate by package weight at checkout.

UPS rates calculate by package weight at checkout.

UPS cannot deliver to PO Boxes or APO, FPO, and DPO military addresses.

Seasonal Ordering

Order early during high-volume holiday seasons to avoid carrier delivery delays.

Note: You will receive an order confirmation email once your purchase has been placed and a separate shipping confirmation with tracking details once your order ships. During high-volume periods (e.g., product launches, holidays, promotions), processing times may be slightly longer.

For Undeliverable Packages

This applies to both domestic and international shipping. We use the shipping address you provided on your order. If a package is undeliverable due to an error in the address provided, it is sent back to us by the carrier.

If you still want to receive your package, you must update your address information via email to us at cs@hottimesauces.com or, if you have an account with us, you can log in and change your information. When we receive the package, you will be sent an invoice to pay for the shipment again. Once a shipment has been delivered to a destination, the label becomes null and void. Therefore, you must pay for the shipping again, and the payment for the first shipping label is not refundable.

For International Shipping

International shipping is done on a package/item weight basis. Shipping is done via USPS and is available in First Class International or Priority International. UPS is also an option.

Depending on the time of the year and the method of shipping you choose, it will take up to 2 weeks for the package to get to you.

Customs, Duties, & Taxes: Please note that international orders may be subject to import duties, taxes, and customs fees levied by the destination country. These charges are the responsibility of the recipient and are not included in our shipping rates.

Shipping Liabilities & Delays

While Hot Time Sauces cannot be held liable for in-transit delays, incorrect delivery addresses, or lost/stolen packages, we want you to get your sauce! If your package goes missing, please contact the carrier directly to file a claim. We will gladly provide any tracking documentation or assistance needed to help you resolve the issue with the carrier.
